payload.title: tasks workspaces list prints machine-readable output for scripts
payload.body: Outcome: scripts can read configured and auto-detected workspaces without parsing human text or the config file. Today `tasks workspaces list` only prints text lines (packages/cli/src/cli.ts:823-828 calls runWorkspacesList, packages/cli/src/commands/workspaces.ts:177-197, which returns strings). `tasks pick`, `list`, `stats`, and `diff` already take --json. Because of this gap, a downstream dotfiles script reads ~/.config/tasks-md/workspaces.json directly (its lib/workspace-discovery.sh says so), so it breaks if the config format changes. Acceptance: `tasks workspaces list --json` prints {configured:[{name,root,repos}],detected:[root]}; a test covers empty, configured, and detected cases; README command table lists the flag. Hypothesis: a --json flag lets consumers stop reading the config file. Measurement: `node packages/cli/dist/cli.js workspaces list --json | jq .configured` exits 0. Success: valid JSON with both arrays. Pivot: if JSON shape is contested, add --porcelain (one tab-separated line per workspace) instead. Anchor: CLI Guidelines (clig.dev) machine-readable output.
